_anchors.canvas.w: 64, the project cell, unchanged. A tree is a prop rather than a character and games often draw them larger, but the shared cell is the discipline this project runs on and a subject that only works with more room is a finding.
_anchors.canvas.originX: canvas.w / 2. A tree is bilaterally symmetric about its trunk in a way no body here has been.
_anchors.canvas.originY: canvas.h * 0.83, the base of the trunk, re-derived with body.scale 0.78: the crown reaches ~50 px above it and the roots ~5 px below, which centres the whole arc in the cell with room for the outline.
_anchors.tones.perMaterial: 5. One more than the control and three fewer than the incumbent. TASTE.md 1b names Chrono as the bar for silhouette and value separation, and separation is what a short ramp over a wide value range buys - the same eight tones spread over a narrow dark range is what it does not.
_anchors.frames.walk: 16, and every phase lands on a whole frame at sixteenths (3/16, 5/16, 8/16, 11/16, 13/16). Sixteen rather than twelve because the wind carries three staggered leaf falls, and each needs enough frames to read as a fall rather than as a jump cut.
_anchors.light.x: unit vector from the upper left, held identical across all four probe samples
_anchors.light.curve: 0.75, BELOW linear, and the first sample in the project to go under 1. Above 1 the ramp is spent on the lit half; this tree needs the opposite, because its subject is a dark body with a narrow bright edge. At 1.1 a 14 px trunk was half pale grey-green and read as the lightest thing in the picture, where the reference trunk is the darkest. Under 1 the light end compresses into a stripe.
_anchors.light.y: the y half of light.x's unit vector
_anchors.outline.enabled: ON. Chrono outlines its sprites - that is how they hold at small size against a busy map.
_anchors.outline.inner: on. The joint line plus a five-tone ramp is the pairing this idiom lives on: value separates the planes, the line separates the parts.
_anchors.outline.rim: OFF, for the same reason as the control - a line and a rim are two answers to one question.
_anchors.outline.material: the ink ramp: a violet-black, so the line belongs to the same world as the cool shadows instead of sitting on top of the art as a neutral.
_anchors.body.scale: 0.78, down from 0.86 because the canopy grew. The subject is now ~72 units crown to root flare; at 0.86 it measured y 0..61 and clipped the top. 0.78 brings it to ~56 px and leaves ~3 px for the ring on every side. The tree shrinking as the canopy fills is the honest trade at a fixed 64 px cell, and it is exactly the variable a larger canvas would separate.
_anchors.gait.swing: 0.28 turn = 101 deg. Set by the LARGEST motion in the gait, which is a falling leaf tumbling about 90 deg, not by the branches - they sway about 10 deg and their keys are authored at branch scale and scaled down in the grammar. Run 7 learned that an action needs a bigger amplitude than a walk; this is the same lesson inside a single gait, where two motions three times apart in size share one channel.
_anchors.gait.lift: 26 px, again set by the leaf: it falls 26 px, roughly from the crown to the base of the trunk. The crown bob is about 1 px and is authored as a fortieth of it.
_anchors.texture.speckle: 0. Chrono sprites have no noise; every pixel is placed. Noise is the incumbent idiom’s signature and it is the thing this probe most wants to see the back of.
_anchors.texture.dither: 0 = the hard cut this sample shipped with, and it is the null case: at 0 the dither term is exactly 0 and the render is byte-for-byte what it was. Turned on per subject, never globally, because the weave is an idiom decision and not a fix.
_anchors.texture.lattice: 4. Size of the ordered dither lattice, 2 or 4. MEASURED rather than chosen: a 4x4 weave needs a 4x4 patch of one surface to be visible, and this project s characters have none — the rider at 36 px scores 0.000 on that share, the skeleton 0.080, the kitten 0.068, a kerb 0.432. Switching both outlines off moved it not at all; doubling the body scale moved it to 0.177, so the cause is scale and not the line. 2 is what fits a small body; 4 is for a road or a sky. Read it with the [weave] line of `node bin/bench.ts`.
_anchors.playback.msPerFrame: 75 ms. 16 x 75 = 1200 ms, the longest cycle in the project. Wind is slower than a stride and a gust that resolves in 600 ms reads as a shudder.
_anchors.playback.scale: 3, because 64 x 3 = 192 px on screen, the shared cell size — held identical to gorilla-jump. This is a probe on the ink axis, so everything that is not ink is frozen: a sample that differs in two things measures neither.
_anchors.light.z: -0.2, the most raking light in the repo. Near 0 the lamp grazes the form and the modelling comes back; the incumbent -0.35 puts the centre of every mass two thirds up its ramp, which is how a body ends up mid-toned everywhere at once.
_anchors.gait.depth: 7 px = the cluster row separation. One of the three falling leaves drifts in depth so it passes behind a branch on the way down, which is the only thing in this sample that would have been inexpressible before run 7.
_anchors.gait.roll: 0 = no roll. Turns, and it is a SEPARATE amplitude from gait.swing on purpose: swing is a walk range (0.08 of a turn) and a flip is a whole one. Run 7 spent a walk amplitude on a jump and lost a limb in every frame; one knob across a 12x range would guarantee it a third time.
_anchors.shadow.steps: 8 px, and it is measured rather than chosen: a sweep at 6, 10, 16 and 24 returns the same shadow area from 6 onward. Past a few pixels the ray has left the body and there is nothing more to block it. 8 keeps a small margin over the saturation point.
_anchors.shadow.bias: 0.25 px of depth, and its job changed. It used to guard against a surface shadowing itself, and it could not: acne scales with curvature, so a lone sphere of radius 18 self-shadowed 198 px and still self-shadowed at eight times the tolerance. That case is now settled by identity - a convex part cannot cast onto itself - so the bias only arbitrates a tie between two DIFFERENT parts whose surfaces meet at nearly the same depth. A quarter of a pixel is enough for that, and acne measures zero at every radius and every bias.
_anchors.shadow.strength: 1 ramp step. On a five-tone ramp that is a fifth of the whole range, which is a readable value drop with a hard edge - the shape the ink verdict of 15/08 selected. 0 disables the pass.
_anchors.fill.x: +0.5, opposite the key lamp on the horizontal. A fill placed on the same side as the key lifts the half that is already lit and does nothing for the half that needs it.
_anchors.fill.y: +0.7, from BELOW. This is bounce: light off the ground back up into the underside of a body. Every fill in painting and photography comes from lower than the key for that reason.
_anchors.fill.z: -0.2, barely on the viewer side. A fill that faces the viewer as hard as the key does flattens the form it exists to recover.
_anchors.fill.weight: 0.15, and it is the measured edge rather than a taste. His ink verdict of 15/08 requires BOTH a wide value range and clustered tone regions, and this knob moves them in opposite directions. Swept at 0, 0.10, 0.13, 0.15, 0.17, 0.19 and 0.22: regions improve monotonically, and the tree loses 23% of its value range between 0.15 and 0.17 (0.654 down to 0.504). 0.15 is the largest weight that costs no range on either subject, and it still buys a 7% gain in region size.
